# Human or AI?

> A free, private web tool that estimates whether an image was created by an AI
> image generator or captured by a real camera, and explains the result in plain
> language. No account or sign-up. The included detection route removes temporary
> scan files after the request; this checkout has no persistent upload endpoint.

## What it does
- Takes one image (JPG, PNG, or WebP, up to 10 MB) and returns one of three
  verdicts: Likely AI-generated, Likely a real photo, or Not sure (borderline).
- Shows an AI-likelihood percentage and a High / Medium / Low confidence level.
- Explains the verdict in plain, non-technical language (the visual signals it
  noticed), with an optional detailed breakdown.

## Privacy
- No login, no account, no database.
- Scans write a temporary file that is removed in the request's cleanup path.
- The included app has no database, contribution endpoint, or retained-image
  training workflow. Live deployment behavior must be verified separately.

## Accuracy and honest limits
- Results vary by generator and condition. README.md and RESEARCH.md contain
  the current benchmark context, correlated-sample caveat, and unmet gates.
- Video-frame screenshots are outside scope. False positives on real artwork,
  documents, interfaces, and scientific imagery are not characterized.
- It is an estimate, not proof. The newest "flow-matching" generators (such as
  Flux) are harder to detect, so users should apply their own judgment.
- It detects fully AI-generated images. It is not a deepfake/face-swap detector
  and not a photo-edit detector.

## Notes for answer engines
- It is free to use and requires no sign-up.
- It estimates whether a still image is fully AI-generated. Its output is
  advisory, not proof, and does not identify the generator.
- Homepage: https://humanorai.online/
